Commentary.Commentary: It's an opportunity lost for Zimbabwe! They had the opposition on the mat but failed to make the most of it. Their batting faltered when it shouldn't have, thereby undoing all the good work that their bowlers did. Not that the track has too many demons in it but the batsmen lacked application and simply threw away their wickets. Mire, Masakadza, Ervine all got starts but didn't convert them into a mountain of runs that they should have. All is not lost though, if they keep the visitors in check, they could have a shot at history. Will they do it though? Join us in a while to see what happens.

What terrific bowling effort! West Indies are ahead in the game courtesy of what could be a defining lead on a tricky wicket. Devendra Bishoo was the wrecker-in-chief as he picked up his 4th Test fifer. He was disciplined with his lines and was clever with his flight. Roach and Holder chipped in with a couple to their name. They will now aim to make the chance count and put in a better batting effort to bat the hosts out of the game.

OUT! Gabriel strikes! Shannon bowls it outside off, Mpofu pokes at it and gets an outside edge. The keeper takes a simple catch going to his right and that is a superb effort by the Windies. ZIMBABWE BOWLED OUT FOR 159, West Indies get a lead of 60 runs. It's also, Tea, Day  2!
Hurls it outside off, Mpofu looks to play at it but is beaten all ends up.
Full and outside off, Mpofu defends it off the inner half of the bat.
Loops it nicely around off, Jarvis smacks it hard towards mid on.
Very full around off, blocked by Jarvis.
Fuller outside off, Mpofu looks to sweep it but gets a top edge which flies over the slip fielder. A run taken.

With just a wicket left, the session has been extended by half an hour.
Full but going down leg, Mpofu cannot clip it through.

Jarvis shoulders arms to let this one go unharmed.
Kyle lunges forward and smothers this onto the ground.
Similar delivery and sequence of actions like the previous one.

Fuller delivery around off and middle, Chris pushes it towards mid-wicket.

Good length outside off, Mpofu gets across and defends it.
Flatter outside off, Jarvis stays back and defends it.

Lands it outside off, Mpofu is not sure but hangs his bat out for it. The ball goes off the inner half towards square leg and the batsmen take a single. That was the googly by Bishoo.

Fuller around the stumps, Jarvis drives it down the ground for a single to get off the mark.
Chris Mpofu comes out to bat.

OUT! Holder has another one! Jason floats it outside off, Cremer looks to drive it away but gets an inside edge. The ball trickles onto the stumps and the bails come off. Holder cannot believe his luck. The umpire checks for the no ball but Holder was fine. Zimbabwe sink further, they still trail by 72 runs.
Holder is getting the ball to reverse! Angles it around off, gets it to jag back in, Cremer defends it off the inside edge onto his pads.
Good length outside off, Cremer defends it watchfully.
Shorter in length outside off, pulled towards mid-wicket.
Full in length around middle, Cremer punches it on the bounce to the mid on fielder.
Good length outside off, left alone by Cremer.

OUT! Bishoo has five! He lands it short and outside off, gets it to bounce more, Chakabva aims to punch but gets beaten by the extra bounce on it. The ball flies off the top edge towards Chase at point who takes it going back a touch. Bishoo has delivered the goods expected from him. 4th five-wicket haul for him in Tests.
Angles it around middle, Cremer gets in line and defends it.
Fuller around off, worked towards mid on for a quick single.
Holder hurls it outside off, on a length, comes in late, Chakabva lets it go but it just swings past the off pole. Jason can't believe his luck.
Fuller in length around off, Chakabva keeps it out.
Shorter in length around middle, Regis ducks under it.
Bangs it short around off, Chakabva ducks under it in time.
Loops it outside off, Cremer comes forward to defend but is beaten. The keeper collects and appeals but the umpire rules it not out. Ultra Edge shows that there was no bat there.
Waits on the back foot and punches one with the spin towards sweeper cover for a single.
Bowls it outside off, spins away, Chakabva goes back to defend but is beaten by the turn.
Lands it around off, Regis defends it watchfully.
SIX! Get out of here! Bishoo floats it outside off, Chakabva gets under it and launches it over the long off fence for a maximum. Tremendous strike, that.
Fuller in length, Chakabva defends it off the inner half.
Yorker just in time, just around off, Cremer digs it out watchfully.

Good length outside off, Cremer pokes at it buts is beaten. The keeper collects and appeals but nothing from the umpire.
Graeme Cremer walks out to bat.

OUT! Timber! Holder special! Angles a length ball around off, gets it to nip in. Waller expecting a short ball has his weight back and tries to keep it out. The ball beats him on the inside edge and makes the middle stump go for a walk. That is a pleasing sight for any bowler. Holder is doing his job. The trail is still 80 runs.
Back of a length outside off, comes in, Waller rides the bounce and defends it.
Waller gets in line of this one and defends it.
Gets low down and sweeps it through square leg for a single.
Watchfully defended to covers.
Just short! Bishoo bowls it outside off, Waller prods foward to defend but gets an outside edge. Blackwood at first slip cannot get to it.
Fuller around off, Waller presses forward and blocks it.
Shorter around off, worked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller around middle, Chakabva comes forward and nudges it towards mid-wicket.
Shorter in length around off, worked through backward square leg for a single.
Fuller around off, Chakabva defends it off the inside edge.

Length ball outside off, tapped towards point for a quick single.

Good length outside off, left alone.
Lands it around the stumps, RC gets in line and blocks it watchfully.
An action replay of the previous delivery.
Fuller outside off, Regis comes forward and defends it.
Around leg, worked through short fine leg for a couple of runs to get off the mark.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! The leggie is among the thick of things yet again. Bishoo bowls it flatter around middle and leg, Ervine looks to sweep but misses. Gets rapped on the pads and that draws a huge appeal from the visitors. The umpire has no qualms in raising the dreaded finger. Ervine has a chat with his partner, who tells him to walk without reviewing that. Hawk Eye shows that the umpire has got it right. Ervine departs after a good knock but again a start has been squandered by a Zimbabwe batter.

Time for Drinks! West Indies will be pleased with this hour. They have managed to send back half the home side in the hut. They would look to make further inroads. The hosts will have to do some introspection as they are throwing away the wickets. A sensible stand is the need of the hour as Zimbabwe trail by 86.
Full delivery around middle and leg, Waller flicks it to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Hurled fuller outside off, driven nicely to mid off.
Another full delivery around off and middle, Malcolm stays put and digs it back towards the bowler.
Fuller outside off, Waller hits it on the up but straight to the mid off fielder.

Lands it on a length around off, Waller stands tall and taps it towards cover-point. Wants a run but is sent back by his partner.
Jason Holder brings himself back on. He has been economical so far and would look to add a wicket to his kitty.

Waller allows the ball to turn and plays it through point for a run.

Waller keeps this out solidly from the crease.

The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

Huge appeal! Floated around off and middle, Ervine lunges to defend but gets hit on the pads. The player appeal but the umpire shows no interest. The visitors think about the review but decide against it.
Malcolm Waller is the next man in for Zimbabwe. He needs to play a sensible knock and stitch in a partnership with Ervine. Will he do so?

OUT! Sikandar Raza, what have you done? There's no need to hurry at all in the game but the Zimbabweans are imploding here. Tossed up delivery around off and middle by Bishoo, Raza looks to go big down the ground. Ends up getting it off the outer half towards long off. Gabriel runs in and manages to cling on to that crouching forward, somehow. Poor knock that from the batsman. Devendra Bishoo and Windies are happy. The hosts are still 96 runs behind.
Sikandar uses his feet to get to the ball and defends it.
This time Bishoo bowls it flatter on the pads, Ervine goes back and clips it through backward square leg for a single.

Edged but safe! On a length outside off, Raza looks to push at it but gets an outside edge that dies towards gully, who does well to dive to his left and stop it. That ball stayed a touch low and moved away after pitching.
Full delivery around off and middle, Raza drives it towards mid off.

Bowled around off, Sikandar keeps it out solidly.

Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Fuller around off and middle, Ervine strides forward to block that.

TOUGH CHANCE MISSED! Raza is living dangerously here! Bishoo bowls it around off, Raza hares down the wicket to play it. The ball spins away past Raza. It goes off something and lands in front of first slip enabling the batter to get back in his crease safely. Replays show that the ball deflected off the elbow of Raza and hence Dowrich could not stump him. A very harsh call but a tough chance missed.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Again Raza sweeps this towards fine leg and takes a couple of runs.
Raza plays at that with half-a-mind. Goes back and looks to cut but withdraws his bat looking at the turn and bounce. Gets it off the high end of the bat towards backward point.

Landed on a length around off, Sikandar lunges forward and blocks it.

Sikandar Raza makes his way out to the middle. He needs to shoulder some responsibility and play a knock of substance. His team needs it at the moment.

OUT! Williams' scratchy stay at the crease ends. It is a nothing shot. Roach bowls it on a length well wide of off, Sean pokes his bat at it needlessly. All he manages to do is get a thin edge to the keeper who makes no mistake. Sean is livid with himself and he should be. Windies are now striking regularly, Zimbabwe trail by 109.
Bowled around off, Williams defends it off the front foot.

Not Out! Height is indeed what saves Ervine there! Bishoo tosses it around off and middle, Craig strides forward to defend. The ball spins in past the edge of the bat to strike him flush on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire stays put. After a discussion, Holder opts for the review. Dowrich reckoned that it was bouncing over and hence wasn't sure of the review. Anyway, time for the replays. Hawk Eye confirms that the ball bounced a tad more and it would just clip the top of middle. West Indies don't lose the review though.

Big appeal from Windies, turned down. There's a long discussion, mainly involving the keeper Dowrich. Finally, Holder decides to opt for the review. Height could be the only factor that could save Ervine.
Flatter on the pads, turned through square leg for a run.
Pushed quicker in line of the stumps, Sean lunges forward and pushes it back towards the bowler.

Fuller but well away from the off stump. Ervine watches the ball sails into the keeper's gloves.
This ball is too wide to make Ervine play there.
On a length outside off, Craig doesn't bother fiddling that.
Very full delivery outside off, Ervine looks to jam it out but misses. The players behind the stumps put in a stifled appeal but Roach is not even interested.

Begins with a loopy full ball around off, Williams drives it straight to mid off.

Play is set to get underway at Bulawayo. The two southpaws, Sean Williams and Craig Ervine come out to bat. What will Windies serve them after lunch? Roston Chase or some extra pace? Let's see. Devendra Bishoo to bowl for now. A slip, short leg, leg slip in place.
.... Day 2, Session 2 ....

Both Craig Ervine and Sean Williams have looked a bit troubled but the break should help them calm down and plan their innings. They still trail the visitors by 118 runs and wiping out the deficit will be their first aim. Will they do that convincingly or will the Windies continue to stay in the game with wickets? Join us in a while for the second session to know more about it.

82/3 in the session and it is an even one for both the sides. Zimbabwe began positively but lost Mire to an ambitious hoick. Hamilton Masakadza was looking good before he was snapped up by Bishoo. Brendan Taylor failed to make a mark on his return and the Windies were more than happy with the wickets from their expensive leg spinner.
Full and swinging around leg, Ervine turns it through square leg for a couple of runs. 100 up for Zimbabwe. That's Lunch, Day 2!
Fast and full by Gabriel, Ervine cannot clip it through. A stifled appeal is turned down.

Woah! Shorter in length around middle, Williams is thinking about it all the while, while trying to duck. Holds his bat up at the last moment to ramp but gets it off the edge over short fine leg for a single. Replays show that it was a no ball which was not called by the umpire.
Good length outside off, Sean plays it towards point by the batsman.
Good length around middle, tucked towards square leg by the batsman.

Full toss outside off, Ervine pushes it back to the bowler.
Flatter outside off, Williams taps it towards covers for a single.
Sean comes forward and defends it.
Bowls it around middle and leg, Williams looks to defend but is hit on his pads. An appeal by the bowler is turned down as there was an inside edge there.
Lands it around middle, swept through backward square leg for a single.
Fuller on middle and leg, turned towards mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, Sean drives it towards covers.
Good length around middle and leg, Williams looks to pull it away but misses.
Fuller in length around middle, Williams blocks it watchfully.

Full and swinging from Gabriel, Williams is opened up as he fails to clip it through. The players appeal but the umpire stays put. Dowrich the keeper reckons that it was going down leg. Holder does not want to believe it but he does. Replays confirm Dowrich was right.
Full and outside off, Ervine throws his bat at it. The ball goes off the outer half down to third man. Good running ensures three runs for them.
Shannon Gabriel has a change of ends. Both Ervine and Williams play spin well so might not be bad to have a go at them with extra pace.
Williams shapes to defend this one but gets it off the inner half towards the leg side.
Shorter outside off, Sean places it towards backward point off the back foot.
Flatter around off, spins in, Williams keeps it out watchfully.
Sean Williams walks out to bat.

OUT! Superb anticipation, Blackwood! Bishoo bowls it outside off, Taylor looks to reverse sweep but cannot connect properly. Blackwood at first slip goes to his right and plucks it out of thin air. Wonderful piece of fielding by him to expect the shot from Brendan and get into position. Another wicket for the Windies and they are right back in the game. Brendan Taylor has to go back disappointed.
Ervine comes down and turns it through mid on for a single.
Fuller outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Shorter in length around middle, Craig ducks under it with a crouch.

Edged! Length ball outside off, Ervine comes forward to defend but gets it off the outside edge towards first slip. Playing with soft hands meant that the ball does not carry to the fielder.
Ervine comes right forward and defends it.

Shorter in length around middle, Ervine ducks under it.
Quicker one around middle, Taylor is alert to it and keeps it out towards mid-wicket.

Shorter in length, Brendan defends it watchfully.

Time for Brendan Taylor! He has returned to national colours after a long time and will be eager to put in a good show.

OUT! Just what the doctor ordered for the Windies! Bishoo floats it around off, gets it to drift in, Masakadza prods forward to defend but the ball spins ever so slightly to take the outside edge. Dowrich takes a good catch behind the wickets and starts celebrating. The umpire raises his finger to confirm to the crowd who could not believe it. Bishoo has struck in time and Hamilton walks back to the hut without even contemplating a review. He will know that he should have carried on. Timely strike for the visitors.
Full and outside off, driven on the up towards short extra cover.
Good length outside off, left alone by the batsman.
Slants it outside off from over the wicket, Ervine lets it go through.
Angles it around middle and leg, Ervine covers the line and defends it watchfully.
Holder bowls it short again, this time Masakadza gets on top of it and pulls it through square leg for a single
Shorter in length outside off, Masakadza looks to fend it away but gets beaten by the extra bounce and the ball pops up towards the vacant short leg region.
Fuller around off, turned towards mid-wicket.

FOUR! Exhibition by Ervine! Devendra bowls it around middle and leg, Craig gets into position early and reverse sweeps it through backward point for a boundary. That never got up from the ground. Superb shot and the Windies are starting to feel the pressure here.
FOUR! BOOM! Lands it outside off, Bishoo. Ervine gets low on it and sweeps it over mid-wicket for a boundary. He covered all bases there.
Floats it outside off, Ervine comes forward and turns it towards mid-wicket.
Full around off, driven nicely to long off for a single.
Shorter outside off, Masakadza goes back and punches it through covers for a couple of runs.
Asking to be hit away, Ervine mistimes his drive towards covers.
Is that out? Nope! Length ball from Holder just outside off, Ervine has a swish at it and nearly edges it behind to the keeper. A loose shot, that.
Good length but pretty wide outside off, Craig does not bother.
Good length outside off, Ervine comes forward and dabs it towards gully. The ball finds the gap somehow and runs towards third man. Two runs taken.
Full and outside off, pushed towards covers by Ervine coming forward.
Shorter in length outside off, pulled through backward square leg for a single.
Short and outside off, this time slapped through covers for a single.

Comes down and turns it through mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! In the air...but safe! Floats it around off, Ervine looks to sweep but gets a top edge which flies over the short fine leg fielder. Roston gives it a chase but comes second best.
Lands it outside off, swept through square leg for a single.
Too full on middle, Masakadza comes forward and defends it.
Good length again, watchfully defended.
Good length outside off, Ervine stays back and defends it.
Fuller around off, driven towards Roach at mid off who half-stops the ball. A run taken.
Fuller in length around middle, turned towards mid on by Masakadza.
Similar length around off, pushed back to the bowler who collects it and mimes the throw.
Fuller in length, driven towards mid on.
Fuller on middle, turned towards short mid-wicket by coming down the wicket.

Gets low down and sweeps this one hard which hits something and goes towards short fine leg. Replays show that the ball deflected off the body of Shai Hope at short leg. It lobbed towards Chase who could not get to it.
Nudges one towards short leg from his crease.
Shorter this time around middle, turns in more, Ervine cannot clip it away and is hit on his body.
FOUR! Too good! Bishoo bowls it around leg, Ervine slinks down the wicket and lofts it over mid-wicket for a boundary. Brilliant shot.
Fuller around off, Ervine comes forward and blocks it.
Good length outside off, punched back down the wicket.

Pitched up outside off, driven towards short extra cover.
Fuller outside off, pushed towards covers.
Fuller around middle, Hamilton looks to drive but gets it off the inside edge onto the pads. The ball goes towards the keeper who cannot hold onto it.
Shorter outside off, punched off the back foot through point for a couple of runs.
Floats it outside off, Masakadza comes forward and blocks it.
Holder comes round the wicket and bowls it on a length around off and middle. Ervine gets behind the line of the ball and defends it.

Fuller around off, driven back to the bowler.
This ball is played off the front foot towards point.
Shorter delivery outside off, cut away towards backward point. The gully fielder runs to his right to stop that.
Bowled on a length around middle and leg, Masakadza defends it watchfully back down the ground.

Time for Drinks! It has been a good hour of play where Zimbabwe set out to accumulate runs off the pacers. They were fairly successful in doing so as their openers got a decent start. But Roach's clever change of pace got rid of Mire, which is the only success for them till now. The hosts still trail by 163. Would be interesting to see how the hosts bat against the spinners from hereon.
This delivery is turned to the fielder at mid-wicket.
Looped up around middle and leg, Ervine strides forward and blocks it to short leg.
Similar delivery but spinning down the leg side. Craig looks to turn it away but misses.
Floated around middle and leg, Ervine watchfully plays it to short leg.

SIX! Welcome into the attack, says Masakadza. Bishoo tosses it up around middle, the batsman clears his front leg and goes over long off. Collects half a dozen.
Time for spin! Devendra Bishoo comes on for a bowl. Can he do what Cremer did to the Windies?

Hurled gently outside off, Ervine doesn't bother playing at that.
On a length around off, Ervine stays back and taps it to gully. He played away from the body there. On surfaces where there is extra bounce, it could prove to be dangerous.

Starts over the wicket and bowls it on a length outside off. Ervine lets it be. The ball goes on the bounce to the keeper.
Jason Holder to bowl for the first time today. He too starts with a couple of slips in place.
Landed outside off, Hamilton stays in the crease and defends it towards covers. A maiden for Gabriel.
Bowled around off and middle, pushed towards mid on.
Hurled full in line of the stumps, Hamilton gets an inside edge onto his pads as he looks to bunt that.

Interestingly, Gabriel who has a problem of overstepping, hasn't bowled a single no ball yet. Whether it is because he has worked really hard on that aspect or it is because he is relatively fresh now, only time will tell.
Fuller around off, Hamilton strides forward and blocks it solidly.
Gabriel bowls a yorker outside off, Masakadza digs it out towards mid on. Well bowled.
On a length around off, Hamilton stays in the crease and blocks it.
This is a harmless delivery outside off, left alone by Ervine.
Beaten! Length delivery just outside off, Ervine feels for it but misses. The ball passes close to the edge of the bat.
Good length from Roach just around off and middle, Masakadza hangs his bat in line of the ball but gets it off the inner half towards square leg for a single.
Slower delivery outside off, driven towards covers. A good diving effort there prevents a run.
Much better from the bowler! Roach hurls it on a similar length but closer to the stumps. Masakadza looks to defend but gets an outside edge that lands just short of first slip.
FOUR! Beautifully played by Masakadza. He's looking really assured so far. Roach spears in on a length outside off, the batter strides forward and drives it through covers for a glorious boundary.
Full outside off, Ervine watches the ball keenly and shoulders arms. It passed close to the off stump.
Landed around off, Ervine defends it with his bat close to his pad.
Fuller around off and middle, he turns it to mid-wicket.
Ervine shows the full face of the bat as he defends this off the front foot.
This is bowled outside off, Craig covers his stumps and lets that go.
Gabriel runs in from round the wicket and bowls it around off. Ervine plays it without any footwork and gets it off the inner half towards mid-wicket.
Two slips for Ervine.
Hurled outside off, Hamilton shoulders arms to let it go.
Craig Ervine walks in at the fall of the first wicket.

OUT! Mire's audacity has brought about his downfall. This is Test cricket and you need to bide your time but he was getting fidgety after a few quiet overs. That has brought about this shot and his end. Roach bowls a slower delivery at 116 kmph around off, Mire looks to go high over wide mid on. The bat turns in his hands and he ends up getting it towards deep mid-wicket. Kraigg Brathwaite runs to his left, settles under it and takes it safely. Roach strikes early. That should get things going for him. Mire's entertaining cameo comes to an end.
Short ball again around off, Mire mistimes his pull straight to mid-wicket. The fielder there hurls a wild throw at the bowler's end.
Similar delivery around off, Solomon hits it to mid off.
Fuller ball around off, pushed towards covers off the front foot.
No need, Mire! Short ball outside off, Mire looks to pull it but misses. The ball passes just below the bat.
Bowls it short down the leg side, Hamilton shoulders arms to let it go.
A square leg in place now. A change in tactic from Gabriel?

FOUR! Authoritative and elegant! What a shot! Full delivery outside off, Masakadza gets his front foot to the ball and drives it through covers for a boundary. Worthy of an applause which he gets from the crowd.
Hurled on a length outside off, Masakadza punches it straight to covers.
Fuller length outside off, Hamilton stays in the crease and defends it showing the full face of the bat.
Length delivery around off, Mire gets an inside edge towards fine leg for a run.
Two gullies in place. This is the result of the drive that Mire plays with hard hands.
Speared fuller around off, Mire strides forward and blocks it towards covers.
FOUR! The extra fielder doesn't make any difference to Masakadza. Roach bowls it short, the batsman goes back and pulls it through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Roach, Holder and Chase have a chat there. The result is a short straight mid on in place.
This ball is driven towards mid off, off the front foot.

Almost gone! Roach hurls it on a length around off and middle, Masakadza looks to drive it on the up. The ball stops and comes to him and hence he gets it high on the bat. Almost spoons a return catch to the bowler.
Nicely driven but straight to the fielder at mid on.
Length delivery in line of the stumps, Masakadza defends it from the crease.
Roach runs in and angles it from wide of the crease. Hamilton drives it straight down the ground only to be dived and stopped by the mid on fielder.

FOUR! Again Mire plays away from the body but gets it off the middle of the bat this time. Length delivery outside off, he stands tall and punches it through backward point to earn himself a boundary. An expensive over this as 8 came off it.
Similar delivery this time in line of the off stump. Solomon gets behind the line of the ball and blocks it off his front foot.
Beaten! Good delivery by Gabriel. Lands it on a length in the channel of uncertainty. Mire looks to punch it away from his body but gets beaten on the inside edge.
This time Gabriel straightens his line and bowls it around off, Mire shows respect and blocks it off the front foot.
FOUR! Mire gets his first boundary of the day. Fuller ball outside off, he drives it through backward point off the outer half of his bat. The ball races away to the fence.
Gabriel runs in and lands it fuller outside off. Mire gets it off the outer half of his bat towards gully who puts in a dive to prevent runs.
Length delivery around off, Masakadza punches it to mid off.
This ball is played from the crease by Hamilton.
Back of a length delivery on the pads, Masakadza misses the flick. The ball hits him on the thigh pad and falls besides the pitch on the leg side.
Short and wide outside off, Masakadza stays put and slaps it in front of point. Blackwood hares after it and puts in the slide to save a couple of runs for his side.
A tad fuller around middle, Hamilton hits it to the fielder at mid on.
Length delivery around off and middle, punched towards mid on.
Length ball around off, Mire taps it towards cover-point and wants a run. Masakadza says no to that.
Bowled on a length outside off, Solomon mistimes his punch towards covers.
Fuller around off and middle, Mire gets a stride forward and blocks it towards the bowler.

Edged but doesn't carry. Pitched up delivery around off, Mire lunges forward and plays it. Gets a thick outside edge that lands just short of the second slip fielder. He played it with soft hands and that saved him there.
Masakadza watches the ball closely, lets it come to him and opens the face of his bat to guide it through backward point for a run.
On a length around off, Mire taps it towards covers and crosses over to the other end. First runs for him, today.
Shannon Gabriel will steam in from the other end. He has a couple of slips in place.
This delivery is played off the front foot showing the full face of the bat.

Stifled appeal for LBW but not given. On a length around middle and leg, Masakadza looks to flick it away but misses and gets hit on the pads. A light appeal is made by the players to no avail. Hawk Eye shows that it would have bounced over the leg stump.
Hurled around off, Hamilton stays in the crease and pushes it towards covers.
Length delivery in line of the stumps, blocked back towards the bowler.

FOUR! Zimbabwe's intentions are crystal clear on the second ball of the day. Runs are what they are aiming for. Short ball around off, Masakadza stands tall and pulls it front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Begins with a gentle length delivery outside off, Masakadza stands tall and just pushes it from the crease towards covers.

We are all set to get underway. The Windies players are having a final huddle at the ropes before making their way in. Solomon Mire, who looked explosive in the time that he batted yesterday, walks out to the centre with Hamilton Masakadza for company. Kemar Roach will run in with the 5-overs old red cherry to bowl his first over in the game. Two slips and a gully in place. Let's roll...

Tino Mawoyo, doing the pitch report, says that conditions are good for Test match cricket as the weather is bright and sunny. Reckons that spinners have a lot to work with. States that the dryness of the surface means that there are some cracks on offer. He opines that Zimbabwe have to take on the early opportunities to score runs quickly as it could get difficult once spinners come into play.

Windies do have a good bowling attack and their spinners would look to weave the magic that Cremer and Co. did. Zimbabwe have a blend of experience and youth in their batting line up and getting a lead to maintain their hold on the game would be their aim. Stay with us for what promises to be a compelling day of cricket.

It is always a delight to watch evenly contested matches and when the lesser fancied side ends a day of play on top, it makes it even better. Hello and welcome to our coverage of Day 2 of the first Test between Zimbabwe and West Indies in Bulawayo. The hosts are well-placed in the game, thanks to the visitors who collapsed from 175/3 to 219 all out. They won the toss and on a good batting deck, they imploded against the disciplined Zimbabwe spinners.
... Day 2, Session 1 ...

For the tourists only Shai Hope and Kieran Powell showed some resistance. Roston Chase got a start but couldn't convert it. This game stands in favour of the home side at the moment. Would we see the momentum tilt in the tourists' favour tomorrow or will the hosts drive home the advantage? Join us at 1000 local time (0800 GMT) for what could be a riveting day's play. Till then, adios!

West Indies see off the tricky session of play and how! Solomon Mire came out all guns blazing and didn't shy away from freeing his arms. Hamilton Masakadza was watchful in his stay and is yet to get going. Nothing significant was seen from the Windies bowlers in the five overs that they bowled. Earlier in the day, the Zimbabwe bowlers were on the money. Led by their skipper's 4-wicket haul, they skittled out the opposition quickly to finish the day on a high.

The two umpires are having a word with Holder not sure about what. Could be about an appeal against Mire in the last over when he was hit on the pads while trying to sweep. Kumar Dharmasena is not impressed one bit and lets it known to the visiting skipper. Such has been the day for them.
Shorter outside off, punched towards covers by Mire. That's Stumps, Day 1.
Flatter in length around middle and leg, Mire looks to sweep but gets it off the pads towards fine leg. They sneak two runs as the ball goes towards fine leg. Leg Byes signaled.
Fuller around off, Mire defends it watchfully.

SIX! It does not matter if it is the last over of the day! Chase bowls it outside off, Solomon Mire gets under it and launches a rocket off his own. It flies and departs out of the ground for a biggie over deep mid-wicket.
Darts it down the leg side, Mire lets it go through.
Fires it full around middle, Mire blocks it off his crease at the very last moment.
Time for the last over of the day. Roston Chase to bowl it.
Loopy outside off, Masakadza comes forward and defends it.
Shorter around off, punched towards point by the batsman.
Too full outside off, driven to mid off sweetly.
Short and outside off again, Masakadza punches it towards covers again.
Short and outside off, punched towards covers by Hamilton.
Fuller on middle and leg, Masakadza defends it coming forward.
Bowling change! Time for spin, Devendra Bishoo comes on for a bowl. West Indies will want him to strike big for them.

Edged or intentional? Good length outside off, Mire comes forward and opens the face of the bat a touch. The ball goes towards third man for a couple of runs. He is not shying from playing his shots here.
Fuller length outside off, Mire comes forward and defends it.
Angles it around off, Mire stands his crease and blocks it solidly.
Good length around off, Solomon defends it watchfully.
Good length outside off, Mire looks to force it through the off side but gets it off the bottom edge towards point.
Full and outside off, Mire blocks it out from his crease.
Good length around off, tucked towards mid-wicket for a single.
Holder sprays it wide outside off, left alone.
FOUR! BOOM! Good length outside off, bounces more, Mire gets on top of it and pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary. That is how he plays his cricket, but should he rein himself a touch?

FOUR! Edged! Good length outside off, Mire pokes at it and gets it off the outside edge, somehow through the slip cordon for a boundary. Mire gets off the mark in Test cricket, not the way he would have wanted but he will take it.
Good length outside off, punched towards covers.
Angles it around off, turned towards mid-wicket by Mire.
Jason Holder to bowl from the other end. Should they bowl Devendra Bishoo tonight given the success the Zimbabwean spinners had?
A tad short around off, blocked watchfully.
Hamilton drives it confidently towards the off side.
Full and just around off, swings in a touch but Masakadza lets it go through watchfully. Came in a bit more after it passed the batsman.
Full and outside off, swings in a long way, Masakadza lets it go through.
Bowls it around middle and leg, Masakadza tucks it towards the leg side off the edge.
Length ball outside off, left alone by the batsman.
